kaps_punt: Rotse - die oppervlak van die Aarde word 'n kors genoem, en bestaan uit rotse (selfs onder die see), en grond; grond, lug, water en sonlig ondersteun lewe op Aarde. Grond kom van rotse af - die land bestaan uit rotse, ondergrond en bogrond; grond ondersteun die lewe op Aarde; bogrond lê op die oppervlak, en bogrond word gevorm wanneer die rotse in klein korrels breek met verloop van tyd.

items.bewering: Op baie plekke langs 'n pad steek kaal rots bo die grond uit. Daardie rots is 'n stukkie van die laag wat om die hele Aarde loop.
items.bron: Encyclopedia.com 'crust' (crust is Earth's outer solid rock shell, about 5 km under oceans to about 60 km under mountains); Lumen Learning Physical Geography 'Soil Horizons and Profiles' (bedrock, R horizon, lies beneath the soil). An outcrop in a road cutting is exposed bedrock, part of the crust.

items.bewering: Die Aarde se oppervlak is daardie buitenste laag, en ons noem dit die kors.
items.bron: Encyclopedia.com 'crust'; JoVE 'Earth's crust' (thin outermost layer of solid rock, continental and oceanic). Strictly the surface is the top of the crust, but equating the two is the curriculum's own wording and does not mislead at this level.

items.bewering: Die kors is van rots gemaak, en die see lê in 'n groot holte daarin.
items.bron: EBSCO Research Starters 'Ocean basins' (ocean basins are depressions floored by basaltic oceanic crust); JoVE 'Earth's crust' (oceanic crust is thinner and denser and lies lower than continental crust). The mapping of 'holte' to an ocean basin holds: the water sits in a low part of the same rock layer.

items.bewering: Die rots loop onder die land deur en ook onder die see deur. Die see is dus nie 'n gat sonder 'n bodem nie.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Oceanic crust' and EBSCO 'Ocean basins' (continental crust under land, basaltic oceanic crust under the sea). The lesson does not claim the rock is the same kind in both places, so nothing false follows.

items.bewering: Die seebodem self is op die meeste plekke 'n dik laag modder en sand bo-op daardie rots.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Oceanic crust' (top layer of oceanic crust is terrigenous or pelagic sediment averaging about 0.5 km thick, over pillow basalt); NOAA NCEI 'Total Sediment Thickness of the World's Oceans and Marginal Seas' (global sediment cover mapped over the ocean floor). Note for the writer, not a fault: sediment is thin or absent near mid-ocean ridges, the deep sea floor is mostly fine mud or ooze, and sand lies mainly near the coasts. 'Op die meeste plekke' and 'modder en sand' hold as a Grade 5 simplification.

items.bewering: Op baie plekke lê 'n laag grond bo-op die rots van die kors. Die laag grond lê nie oral ewe dik nie.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Catena (soil)'; EGU2015-7704 field study (soil depth varies across a hillslope, shallower at the top and deeper downslope).

items.bewering: Op 'n koppie kan die rots op plekke heeltemal kaal lê. In 'n vallei kan die grond baie diep wees.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Catena (soil)'; EGU2015-7704 (soil depth shallower near the top of a catchment and increasing downslope). The word 'kan' is right: the pattern is common but not universal, as a southern Italian catena study shows.

items.bewering: Jy kan dus nie van bo af sê hoe diep die rots onder jou voete lê nie.
items.bron: Follows from the catena sources above. EGU2015-7704 calls soil depth 'notoriously difficult' to quantify on a hillslope.

items.bewering: Grawe 'n gat in die tuin en die grond lyk anders soos jy dieper kom. Op die meeste plekke bestaan die land uit drie lae wat bo-op mekaar lê.
items.bron: Lumen Learning Physical Geography 'Soil Horizons and Profiles' (horizons differ in colour and make-up with depth: topsoil A, subsoil B, partly weathered C, bedrock R; not every profile has all of them). Topsoil, subsoil and rock is the standard simplification and the curriculum's own three layers.

items.bewering: Bogrond lê heel bo op die oppervlak, en die meeste plante het hulle wortels daarin.
items.bron: Lumen Learning 'Soil Horizons and Profiles' (A horizon is where most plant roots grow); Corteva 'Understand the 3 soil layers underfoot' (topsoil is the main root zone; roots reach the subsoil less densely).

items.bewering: Daaronder lê die ondergrond, en party plante se wortels kom tot so diep. Heel onder lê die rots wat die twee lae grond dra.
items.bron: Lumen Learning 'Soil Horizons and Profiles' (subsoil beneath topsoil, bedrock at the base); Corteva soil-layer page (many plants have roots that reach the B horizon).

items.bewering: Vryf 'n handvol bogrond tussen jou vingers en jy voel baie klein korrels. Daardie korrels was lank gelede deel van harde rots.
items.bron: Lumen Learning 'Soil Horizons and Profiles' (mineral particles in soil, sand, silt and clay, come from the weathering of parent rock; bedrock slowly breaks down and feeds the soil above).

items.bewering: Rots breek stadig in kleiner stukkies totdat net sulke korrels oorbly.
items.bron: Lumen Learning 'Soil Horizons and Profiles' (C horizon is partly broken-down rock; weathering slowly reduces bedrock to soil particles).

items.bewering: 'n Plant se wortel druk in 'n bars in en maak dit wyer.
items.bron: OpenGeology glossary 'root wedging' (roots grow into existing cracks in bedrock and widen them); University of Washington news on roots breaking up rock and speeding soil production. The lesson rightly has the root go into an existing crack rather than break solid rock.

items.bewering: Bedags maak die son se hitte die rots warm, en snags koel dit weer af. Dag na dag laat die hitte en die koue die rots uiteindelik bars.
items.bron: Eppes et al. 2010, Geomorphology, 'Cracks in desert pavement rocks: further insights into mechanical weathering by directional insolation'; SERC Carleton 'Cracking up: emerging evidence for the importance of the sun in the mechanical weathering of rocks'; Eppes and Magi acoustic-emission records, AGU 2014 (most cracking recorded on warm days). Heating and cooling stresses arise daily and do crack rock over time. Older lab work (Griggs 1936) doubted how much it matters, but recent field evidence supports it. The lesson claims only that it happens, not that it is the main cause, and that holds.

items.bewering: Rots verander so stadig in bogrond dat 'n mens dit nie kan sien gebeur nie. 'n Nuwe laag bogrond het baie langer nodig om te vorm as wat 'n mens lewe.
items.bron: FAO Director-General, speech to the 145th FAO Council, 5 December 2012 (forming one centimetre of soil can take up to a thousand years); FAO Family Farming Knowledge Platform (2 to 3 cm of fertile soil can take up to 1 000 years). Even at the fastest rates a whole layer takes far longer than a human lifetime.

items.bewering: Bogrond is ook nie net gebreekte rots nie. Daar is nog ander goed in die grond.
items.bron: Lumen Learning 'Soil Horizons and Profiles' (topsoil mixes mineral particles with humus or organic matter).

items.bewering: Grond, lug, water en sonlig ondersteun saam die lewe op die Aarde. Saam hou hierdie vier dinge die lewe op die Aarde aan die gang.
items.blok: Vier dinge wat die lewe ondersteun
items.bron: Smithsonian Environmental Research Center (serc.si.edu): photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide from air, water and light; soil supplies water and minerals. The curriculum's own statement, and true as a general claim about life on land.

items.bewering: Plante staan met hulle wortels in die grond en kry water en voedingstowwe daaruit. Die plant maak sy eie kos met sonlig, nie uit die grond nie.
items.blok: Vier dinge wat die lewe ondersteun
items.bron: Smithsonian Environmental Research Center (carbon dioxide + water + light -> sugar + oxygen); MSU archive, 1931 agricultural article (plants take their mineral nutrients from the soil solution). Soil supplies water and minerals but no food energy, so the contrast drawn here is correct and avoids the common misconception.

items.bewering: Die lug gee die suurstof wat mense en baie diere met elke asemteug inasem.
items.blok: Vier dinge wat die lewe ondersteun
items.bron: American Museum of Natural History, 'Life in Water: Vertebrates - Breathing' (air-breathers take oxygen from air; fish take oxygen dissolved in water through gills). 'Baie diere' rather than 'alle diere' is correctly narrowed.

items.bewering: Plante en diere kan ook nie sonder water lewe nie.
items.blok: Vier dinge wat die lewe ondersteun
items.bron: Smithsonian Environmental Research Center (water is an input to photosynthesis); AMNH breathing resource (animal life depends on water). True as a general claim.

items.bewering: kors: Die buitenste laag rots wat om die hele Aarde loop.
items.bron: Encyclopedia.com 'crust'; JoVE 'Earth's crust' (outermost layer of solid rock, under both continents and oceans).

items.bewering: oppervlak: Die buitekant van iets.
items.bron: Standard dictionary sense of 'oppervlak' (the outside or top face of something), matching English 'surface' as in Encyclopedia.com's use for Earth's crust. A word definition, not a scientific claim.

items.bewering: bogrond: Die boonste laag grond waarin die meeste plante hulle wortels het.
items.bron: Lumen Learning 'Soil Horizons and Profiles'; Corteva soil-layer page (topsoil is the upper layer and the main root zone).

items.bewering: ondergrond: Die laag grond tussen die bogrond en die rots daaronder.
items.bron: Lumen Learning 'Soil Horizons and Profiles' (subsoil B horizon lies below topsoil and above parent material and bedrock). Leaving out the partly weathered C layer is an acceptable simplification.

items.bewering: korrel: 'n Baie klein stukkie van 'n vaste stof, soos rots.
items.bron: Standard dictionary sense; consistent with Lumen Learning's description of soil mineral particles (sand, silt, clay) as small pieces of weathered rock.

items.bewering: voedingstowwe: Stowwe wat 'n plant of 'n dier nodig het om te lewe en te groei.
items.bron: Smithsonian Environmental Research Center and MSU 1931 agricultural article (plants need soil minerals such as nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium to grow). Animals take in nutrients from food. The definition is accurate and wide enough for both.

opsomming: Every checkable claim held up against sources. The two points closest to the line are both acceptable as written. Sediment on the sea floor is thin near the mid-ocean ridges and is mostly fine mud rather than sand in the deep sea, so 'op die meeste plekke' holds. Day-and-night heating cracking rock was long doubted, but recent field research supports it, and the lesson claims only that it happens.
